summary: The recorded base reproduced real PyZMQ descriptor exhaustion after 38 unique endpoints under RLIMIT_NOFILE=128. The exact candidate completed 100 endpoints with cache and monitor maps bounded at 21, and independently applied backpressure when every cached endpoint had an active sender lock.

tests.what_was_measured: Actual PyZMQ behavior with RLIMIT_NOFILE=128: ZMQError Too many open files after 38 endpoints, 38 cached PUSH sockets, 38 monitors, and 127 open descriptors. The probe reports the caught failure and exits zero.
Actual PyZMQ behavior with RLIMIT_NOFILE=128 and cache size 21: 100 connections completed, 21 PUSH sockets and monitors retained, 76 descriptors open, no exception.
Candidate regression coverage; 9 tests passed, including real low-FD churn, active-sender backpressure, LRU reuse, paired cleanup, and atomic monitor failure handling.
Independent adversarial case: fifth endpoint blocked while all four cached sender locks were active, then completed after one release with the cache still bounded at four and no error.
Environment-field compatibility; 13 tests and 2 subtests passed.

gpu_execution.evidence: The defect and candidate changes are in the CPU/PyZMQ connection cache. The prepared environment is ROCm 7.2, not the reporter's 16x NVIDIA H800 environment; no GPU claim is made.

remaining_limitations: The reporter's 16x NVIDIA H800, multi-node, full-model serving workload and weights were unavailable; only the issue-specific host-side ZMQ contract was reproduced.
An explicitly oversized SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_ZMQ_SOCKET_CACHE_SIZE can exceed the descriptor budget because explicit configuration overrides the derived default.
Persistent descriptor exhaustion caused by unrelated process components remains possible and is not masked by the bounded one-second transient EMFILE retry.
